title: The Millau Viaduct's tallest pier stands 13 m higher than the Eiffel Tower

cover.alt: The Millau Viaduct's slender piers and fan of white cables carrying a motorway high above the village of Creissels and the Tarn valley.

body: The **Millau Viaduct** carries the A75 motorway 2,460 m across the Tarn valley in southern France, with the road about 270 m above the valley floor. Its pier P2 rises 343 m to the tip of its mast, 13 m more than the 330 m Eiffel Tower, which makes it the tallest structure in France; the bridge itself was the tallest in the world for over two decades. Designed by the engineer Michel Virlogeux and the architect Norman Foster, it was built in just over three years, from 16 October 2001 to its opening on 16 December 2004, for about €394 million. Its 36,000-tonne steel deck was never lifted into place: assembled on the plateaus at both ends, it was pushed out over the piers by hydraulic rams, 600 mm per four-minute cycle, resting on temporary towers until the two halves met.
